re_line: Chinese firm buys $1bn of PNG mines and ports · NZ Treasury: Luxon and Peters bypassed Cabinet on Forum hosting · Fletcher says Beijing turning 'smug' · PNG court forces Solwara disclosure · Rinehart backs Hanson against Hastie
morning_memo: A Chinese company has spent more than $1 billion buying mines and port facilities across three Papua New Guinea islands, extending Beijing's commercial footprint in a resource sector Canberra and Washington are also courting.

New Zealand's Treasury has disclosed that Christopher Luxon and Winston Peters committed the country to hosting the 2027 Pacific Islands Forum without Cabinet approval, and told ministers the bid's value for money is not clear.

Papua New Guinea's Supreme Court has ordered the state to hand over documents on the Solwara deep sea mining project, setting a disclosure precedent seven years after customary landowners went to court.

top_stories.headline: Chinese company buys Papua New Guinea mines and port facilities for more than $1 billion
top_stories.body: A Chinese company has spent *more than $1 billion* on mines and port facilities across three islands in Papua New Guinea, Islands Business reported, in a transaction tagged to the Simberi operation. The purchase bundles extraction assets and logistics infrastructure in a single deal. The China in the Pacific ledger last recorded a PRC-related PNG development on September 5, when five leaders were absent from the Palau summit as Australia's treaty run reached Fiji.
top_stories.src_line: per Islands Business: "Chinese firm buys PNG gold mine"

top_stories.headline: Former ambassador says Beijing growing 'smug', faults Coalition's response to coercion
top_stories.body: **Graham Fletcher**, Australia's ambassador in Beijing from 2019 to 2023, said some Coalition MPs seemed "almost delighted" at being targeted by China and "paraded" the list of 14 grievances handed over by Chinese diplomats. His posting spanned the collapse of bilateral ties in 2020-21 and the relationship's stabilisation after Labor's 2022 election win. Fletcher also said China under **Xi Jinping** is increasingly "smug" and closed off to new ideas, warning that ideological fixations risk sapping the country's entrepreneurial drive.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Former China ambassador warns Beijing is becoming 'smug' and closed"

top_stories.headline: Rinehart backs Hanson's campaign against Hastie
top_stories.body: **Gina Rinehart** once supported the Liberal MP **Andrew Hastie** and has now thrown her support behind **Pauline Hanson** and One Nation's plan to bring him down, the Sydney Morning Herald reported. The feud escalated this week over a One Nation animated cartoon labelling the former SAS officer a "traitor", which Hanson has refused to withdraw. The RSL has made a rare political intervention in Hastie's defence.
top_stories.src_line: per Sydney Morning Herald: "Why Rinehart is pushing to make Hastie an outcast, and backing Hanson to bring him down"

overnight_items.headline: Rudd warns Australia risks becoming a 'second-rate country'
overnight_items.body_text: **Kevin Rudd** told the National Press Club that Australia risks becoming a "second-rate country" without a "radical change in our national psychology". The address, replayed on ABC Radio National Breakfast, framed complacency as a strategic problem rather than a domestic one. Rudd separately recounted how a network of senior businessmen arranged his introduction to the Pfizer chief Albert Bourla.

overnight_items.headline: Universities rebel against national security rules for research
overnight_items.body_text: Australian universities are clashing with the federal government over new national security rules governing research, The Australian reported. The rules cover the same technology-protection and foreign-collaboration terrain that underpins Australia's science cooperation with the United States and United Kingdom. No resolution timetable was reported.

overnight_items.headline: Albanese moves on migration after Burke speech cancelled
overnight_items.body_text: **Anthony Albanese** is scrambling to take the heat out of the migration debate after a speech by Home Affairs Minister **Tony Burke** was cancelled, the Sydney Morning Herald reported. The paper frames the plan as an attempt to draw in Opposition Leader **Angus Taylor** while squeezing One Nation. Migration policy has dominated the past week of federal argument alongside the Hastie dispute.

overnight_items.headline: Australia marks 25 years since the September 11 attacks
overnight_items.body_text: Australia, the United States, and the rest of the world marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks. ABC Radio National carried an interview with former prime minister **John Howard**, who was in Washington on the day, as part of its anniversary coverage.

aukus_watch.headline: British envoy fields questions on UK yard capacity for SSN-AUKUS timetable
aukus_watch.body_text: Acting British High Commissioner to Australia **Dr Brian Jones** discussed defence budgets, shipyard capacity, and the timetable for Australia's submarine acquisition on ABC's Global Roaming, five years after AUKUS was announced. The programme noted that while most debate centres on the United States and the promised Virginia-class boats, the ultimate goal is the British-designed vessels. Jones was also asked how the United Kingdom views China's increasing forays into the Pacific.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG Supreme Court orders release of Solwara deep sea mining documents
pacific_wire.body_text: Opponents of the Solwara deep sea mining project won a further ruling requiring Papua New Guinea's government to release project documents. The Centre for Environmental Law and Community Rights sued the Mineral Resources Authority and the Conservation and Environtment Protection Authority in 2019; a 2024 Supreme Court order to hand over the mining licence and environmental permit has still not been met by the Mineral Resources Authority. CELCOR executive director **Peter Bosip** called the delays "a delayed tactic by the MRA and SEPA to suppress the customary landowners".

pacific_wire.headline: Pilot track opens on 1,300km road linking Port Moresby and Lae
pacific_wire.body_text: Papua New Guinea's government has opened a pilot track on a new road connecting Port Moresby to Lae, spanning *1,300 kilometres*. Prime Minister **James Marape** made the drive of more than 18 hours across the mainland in a ministerial convoy. The route is intended to carry essential supplies between the country's two largest cities.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG launches HPV vaccination targeting 60,000 girls in first phase
pacific_wire.body_text: Papua New Guinea has begun an anti-cervical cancer vaccination programme whose first phase is expected to reach about *60,000 eligible girls*. Alongside school-based delivery, the government will run the programme through health facilities and community outreach so that girls who are out of school or far from services are not left behind.

pacific_wire.headline: Samoa approves pilot on online voting for citizens overseas
pacific_wire.body_text: Samoa's government has approved a pilot project to investigate how Samoans living abroad could cast votes online, reviving a contested debate over diaspora suffrage. **Teleiai Edwin Puni**, a chief based in New Zealand, said diaspora votes would add value to Samoa's development, noting that many who left to find opportunities were "always contributing back to Samoa". Opinion is mixed both among residents and the diaspora.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji's prime minister denies lobbying chiefs to delay the general election
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji's prime minister denied lobbying the Great Council of Chiefs to delay the general election, PACNEWS reported. A separate item in the same bulletin said the Constitutional Review Commission's report is unlikely to affect the election timetable. Transparency Solomon Islands used the bulletin to argue that democracy "does not end at the ballot box".

pacific_wire.headline: Tonga's deputy PM says no community is too remote for an effective warning
pacific_wire.body_text: Tonga's deputy prime minister told a regional gathering that no community is too remote to receive an effective early warning, as PACNEWS reported calls for stronger Pacific warning systems in the face of growing climate risk. Another item in the bulletin reported that Pacific climate plans may rest on the wrong picture of rising sea levels, and that justice leaders have been urged to unite against organised crime.

pacific_wire.headline: Forum urged to widen the Regional Action Plan on Peace and Security
pacific_wire.body_text: An Islands Business commentary argues the Pacific Islands Forum has "an important opportunity to ensure that the Regional Action Plan on Peace and Security does more", tying peace to climate, justice, and inclusion rather than a narrow security frame. The piece follows the Koror leaders meeting.

new_zealand.headline: Treasury says Luxon and Peters committed New Zealand to hosting the 2027 Forum without Cabinet approval
new_zealand.body_text: **Christopher Luxon** and **Winston Peters** did not consult Cabinet before committing New Zealand to host the Pacific Islands Forum in 2027, the Treasury said. Budget 2026 committed *$20 million* across this year and next for the summit, with Peters making the offer at a Forum Foreign Ministers meeting in August of last year and the official announcement following in September. March advice to Finance Minister **Nicola Willis** recommended excluding a NZ$30m funding proposal, said "Cabinet approval was not sought before announcement of the hosting arrangement", and that "the value for money of the bid is not clear"; Willis was separately advised to cut the package to $10m, closer to the cost of hosting in 2011, since "$6.4m for policy work" was discretionary or scalable.

canberra_politics.headline: The Australian reports Labor premiers in open revolt against Albanese
canberra_politics.body_text: The Australian's Inquirer section reports Labor premiers in open revolt and argues **Anthony Albanese**, after an easy run, is now rattled. The piece lands in a week dominated by federal grant controversies, migration argument, and a Queensland credit downgrade.

canberra_politics.headline: Reshuffle chatter builds in Labor ranks despite settled ministry
canberra_politics.body_text: Albanese has not turned his mind to his next ministry, which is unlikely before 2027, but Labor MPs are already canvassing a reshuffle, the Sydney Morning Herald reported. Any rearrangement would eventually reach the defence, foreign affairs, and Pacific island affairs portfolios.

canberra_politics.headline: Labor's $75m anti-extremism programme failing most participants, paper reports
canberra_politics.body_text: The government's flagship *$75 million* anti-extremism programme is failing to reform the vast majority of its participants, The Australian reported. The finding lands as police investigate a man filmed throwing pork products at a mosque in Warragul, Victoria.

business_economy.headline: Queensland credit rating downgraded for the first time in 17 years
business_economy.body_text: Queensland's credit rating has been cut for the first time in 17 years, The Australian reported, with the paper saying Premier **David Crisafulli** is turning a blind eye to debt. The downgrade was described as imminent in yesterday's reporting and is now confirmed.

business_economy.headline: Houthis take Mocha and press towards Bab el-Mandeb as Brent holds above $100
business_economy.body_text: Iran-aligned Houthis seized the Yemeni port city of Mocha and reached the Hanish Islands overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, while Iranian strikes damaged United States fighter aircraft at a base in Jordan. Control of the strait would give Iran leverage over a second major energy transit corridor. Brent stood at *104.08*, up 6.29 percent.

business_economy.headline: Greens and Coalition unite to block passenger tax rise
business_economy.body_text: The Greens and the Coalition will combine to block the federal government's increase to the passenger movement charge, The Australian reported, leaving the measure dead on arrival in the Senate. The revenue was booked in the government's forward estimates.

business_economy.headline: Energy ministers agree to explore lifting Australia's plug-in solar ban
business_economy.body_text: Australia's energy ministers agreed to explore pathways for the "safe deployment" of plug-in solar and batteries, a step towards lifting a ban that keeps the technology from apartment dwellers and renters. The United Kingdom legalised balcony solar last month and New Zealand has flagged plans to do the same within 12 months. Campaigners want a timeline by December.

business_economy.headline: Modelling warns budget changes will wipe $1bn from GDP and lift rents
business_economy.body_text: Modelling reported by The Australian warns federal budget changes will wipe *$1 billion* from GDP and push rents up by five times the increase claimed by Treasurer **Jim Chalmers**. The Treasurer's own figures on the measure have not been revised.

primary_documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand
primary_documents.headline: Thailand confirms envoy attended the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting in Palau
primary_documents.body_text: Thailand's foreign ministry published a readout confirming that the Chairman of the Advisory Board to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs attended the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting in the Republic of Palau. The Koror meeting ran from August 30 to September 4, 2026, and passed the Forum chair to Palau.

calendar_watch.event: Advance voting opens for New Zealand's general election
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Three weeks of early voting begin with foreign and Pacific policy questions, including the Forum hosting commitment, already in dispute.
Decides whether the National, ACT, and NZ First coalition, and Winston Peters' foreign policy, continue.

calendar_watch.event: New Zealand hosts the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Treasury has told ministers the hosting costs are unavoidable but that there is significant scope to manage them down.
President Donald Trump said he expects the Iran war to end after the midterms, a timeline with direct consequences for oil and shipping.
The next round will test United States pressure for higher Australian defence spending and the shape of force posture cooperation.

key_stat.label: Chinese purchase of PNG mines and port facilities
key_stat.context: A single Chinese transaction covering assets across three Papua New Guinea islands exceeds a billion Australian dollars, in a sector Canberra and Washington are also courting.

also_today.headline: Mobility provisions in recent Australia-Pacific bilateral agreements
also_today.body_text: **Jane McAdam** writes that beyond Tuvalu's climate visa, six Australia-Pacific agreements now recognise mobility as a tool for adaptation, security, and dignity. The piece reads the agreements against Pacific leaders' 2023 endorsement of the Pacific Regional framework on mobility.

also_today.headline: China is poised to lead in research on quantum technologies. Democracies must act
also_today.body_text: ASPI research finds China is either already ahead or poised to take the lead in quantum technologies, and argues Australia and its democratic partners must act promptly to avoid conceding that lead. Quantum sits inside AUKUS Pillar 2.

also_today.headline: Scientists put Lae fault line closer to the city centre than thought
also_today.body_text: Scientists in Papua New Guinea say there is a one-in-four chance a fault line at Lae produces a quake of magnitude 8.5 within the next 50 years, and that the fault runs closer to the central business district than previously understood.

also_today.headline: Tonga preparedness push leans on traditional knowledge and language
also_today.body_text: Disaster managers in Tonga say constant reminders are needed even where disasters are frequent, and that the language used in warnings adds vital context. The programme is produced by ABC International Development with funding from the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.
